explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a Go-based MCP (Model Context Protocol) service that automates interactions with the Xiaohongshu website via a headless browser.  
   - It exposes a JSON-RPC/HTTP interface (“MCP server”) for AI clients (Claude, Cursor, VSCode, Gemini, etc.) to call tools like check_login_status, publish_content, list_feeds, search_feeds, get_feed_detail, post_comment_to_feed.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level Go binaries:
     • main.go + app_server.go + routes.go + handlers_api.go + mcp_handlers.go + service.go + middleware.go + streamable_http.go → compose the HTTP/MCP server  
     • cmd/login/main.go → CLI tool to perform an initial manual login in a browser window  
   - Domain-specific package: xiaohongshu/ → browser automation for login, feeds, publish, comments  
   - Utilities:  
     • pkg/downloader → image download & processing  
     • cookies/cookies.go → persistence and retrieval of session cookies  
     • configs/*.go → runtime configuration (headless flag, image settings, username)  
   - Static assets + docs + examples illustrate usage and integration.  

3. Extract key architectural insights from README  
   - The service starts a headless Chrome (or non-headless when ‑headless=false) and holds cookies in local storage.  
   - Exposes an HTTP endpoint at localhost:18060/mcp implementing the MCP JSON-RPC API.  
   - AI clients register the MCP server and invoke “tools” mapped to specific handlers in mcp_handlers.go.  
   - Each tool handler calls into service.go, which in turn drives the xiaohongshu package that executes browser tasks to perform actions on the real website.

4. Creating the system design diagram  
   a. Main components  
     1. Clients: Claude Code CLI, Cursor, VSCode, Gemini CLI, Inspector  
     2. HTTP/MCP Server (main.go + HTTP router + JSON-RPC layer)  
     3. API Handlers (handlers_api.go → generic HTTP; mcp_handlers.go → protocol mapping)  
     4. Service Layer (service.go)  
     5. Domain/Browser Adapter (xiaohongshu/*)  
     6. Infrastructure: Headless Chrome / Browser driver (browser/browser.go)  
     7. Utilities: Cookie Store, Image Downloader, Config loader  
     8. External System: Xiaohongshu.com website  

   b. Relationships & data flow  
     - Client sends JSON-RPC over HTTP → HTTP/MCP Server  
     - Router forwards to appropriate handler → Handler calls Service Layer  
     - Service invokes Domain Adapter → Domain Adapter issues browser commands → Chrome navigates to Xiaohongshu → returns HTML/JSON  
     - Service processes the result → Handler marshals it back to JSON-RPC response → back to Client  
     - Cookie Store is read/written by Domain Adapter to maintain session between calls  

   c. Architectural patterns & principles  
     - Layered architecture: Presentation (HTTP/MCP & routing) → Application (Handlers) → Business (Service) → Integration (xiaohongshu adapter) → Infrastructure (Browser)  
     - Adapter pattern for decoupling the Service logic from the browser automation details  
     - Dependency injection via configs package and middleware  
     - Clear separation of concerns: downloader, cookies, browser, handlers  

   d. Key technologies & frameworks  
     - Go standard library for HTTP, JSON-RPC handling  
     - Chromedp or a custom browser driver (browser/browser.go) for headless Chrome automation  
     - Model Context Protocol (MCP) over HTTP  
     - JSON-RPC 2.0  
     - Go modules (go.mod)  
     - File-based cookie persistence  

5. Tailoring the diagram for this full-stack service-style tool  
   - Emphasize the separation between:  
     • MCP protocol layer vs. native HTTP endpoints  
     • Business logic (service.go) vs. browser integration  
     • CLI login tool (cmd/login) as a one-off manual setup component  
   - Highlight how AI clients dynamically discover “tools” via the MCP tool registry  

6. Diagramming guidelines  
   - Components as clearly labeled boxes:  
     • Use a distinct color for “MCP/HTTP Server”  
     • Another color for “Service & Handlers”  
     • Yet another for “Browser Automation”  
     • Cylinder icon for Cookie Store  
     • Cloud icon for External Website (xiaohongshu.com)  
   - Directional arrows for request/response flows:  
     • Client → MCP Server → Handler → Service → Adapter → Browser → Website  
     • Website → Browser → Adapter → Service → Handler → Client  
   - Annotate data formats on arrows (HTTP/JSON, JSON-RPC, HTML pages, images)  
   - Group related packages in swimlanes or layered zones  

7. Essential details to capture  
   - “cmd/login” as a separate sub-flow for initial authentication  
   - Headless vs. non-headless mode toggle  
   - The six MCP tools as sub-components of mcp_handlers.go  
   - The cookie persistence mechanism that underpins session continuity  

By modeling this layered design with clear labels, color-coded zones, and directional arrows for each protocol boundary, you’ll produce an accurate, comprehensive architecture diagram that guides both development and future extension.  
</explanation>
